Core gameplay loop is solid, mechanics are solid. No bugs glitches or crashes. Shockingly solid bones. Now for the meat. No external progression. limited loot pool with "random modifiers" attached. Venders are less of a mechanic and more of a checkmark. Bosses are janky and with it being a voxel game there are issues with hitboxes spells getting stuck on corners ect. Theres a seriously low pool of drops and mobs. Spell components are almost always all on the desert level. All in all I'd give it a 6/10. Grab it on sale, it'll kill a couple of hours.

Wow okai, this is very good. Very interesting spell system, once u learn the runes u can master it with speed. Can still quickly change spells on one staff/wands or settup different staffs/wands with many runes across your hotbar. Spells are not limited to just wizard stuff, can put it on melee or bows. Character freedom on how you level it despite the starter class. Items/weapons are interesting enough, more so later on. voxel terrain destruction is good, get's better after u find a pickaxe and explode rune. Over all art direction is very good. Runs good considering all the simulation. 144 fps all da time, unless i start using an absured amount split/bounce runes. There are insta kill spikes, however not really an issue the modules with them aren't really that difficult. The game is somewhat similar to Barony and vagante which is my addiction - w - , still very different. Has someee small issues thingys though: Cannot rebind toolbar keys Had world start half vanishing untill it crashed once Dual wielding bug where it duplicates the weapon/ cannot take it off to parry. Attack click controls swap on dual welding. (not exactly bad but I don't like) Some mobs like skeleton are braindead and walk into walls. No shields (I didnt find any) Gear minor attributes bascially do nothing (+2% crit chance. woa +1 knockback!, major attributes are fine like free fire rune) and only have one attribute max. Can't mark on the map, must walk there in person Needs more scrolls (missing things like repair scroll, magic mapping ect) Falling short distances does nothing, but just a little more and it drops half your health. Tho these are just small things and one big void crash bug. 8/10 :3

One of the best wizard games I've played in a long-long time! I really love the rune system, kind of reminds me of Arx Fatalis and, surprisingly enough, a bunch of Minecraft mods. The only con is that the enemy AI is very basic, so a lot of the mobs in the earlier floors end up just walking in circles and barely attacking. That issue goes away in the latter floors, however, as the number of enemies goes up exponentially, ending up in a very challenging experience. Also, based af dev made decently easy modding system, props for that!

I want to say that this game is absolutely worth it. It's scratches that itch for a magic-building rougelike. There are an incredible amount of runes that can be applied to your spells, weapons, and even summons. The combos are extremely diverse and fun. Nuking a poor beetle that popped out of a box is extremely satisfying. The game isn't exactly hard persay, but when you're starting out it can be easy to lose your first couple of runs because you are learning what certain things do and what traps to look out for. The game doesn't have any "timed" achievements, the dev knows that you are going to get lost in there. I am posting this review after having achieved my first actual win because I intend to continue playing and trying out using different combos of weapons and runes. If you also like destructible terrain, this game is just gold. But please don't tunnel through the floor because you hear a welcoming noise, you might just accidentally stumble upon the level boss... Good luck and happy casting!
Highly recommend. There's not much to it, but it's cheap and a fun way to pass the time.

Played so many roguelikes I can tell there's inspiration from: Noita, Pixel dungeon games, sandbox elements. This Since it was not early access I expected much more polish but was disappointed by the content. First off, enemies are not difficult, within 1 playthrough I had found many enemies were very easy to defeat just being airborne. Their AI is suited for close quarters damage, so playing any class/putting your skill points into mana recovery just means you kill all slowly bit by bit (not fun). If you decide to go melee, then it may be a bit more interesting until you inevitably run out of healing. The blocking doesn't feel good and still deals massive damage. Next up, the terrain generation is just utterly miserable to play though, the starting stages are just wandering around simulator, too many dead ends. random ravines which don't aid the player, the caves are always cramped and feel barebone. The other levels do feel a bit better but always lead to disappointing dead-ends. This also leads to my point on the map, I've seen better maps on minecraft mods, it doesn't update to player terrain digging, so you have no clue where you are and as soon are not on the same y-level the map for that level is completely gone, I would much rather prefer some holographic 3d map or at least a 2d map with a y-level slider. Classes? I mean seriously calling different types of classes is like joke, you get like 1 or 2 more in that skill area with a weapon of that choice, like at least unique perks please. Lastly, the gameplay loop. Titles similiar to Shattered PD, where identifying items is key, the runes here never change, rings, armour they are always safe to equip (im sure there will be future updates). Once you playthrough like 3 runs, you expect everything. It just becomes, find the boss after walking for miles and repeat. Like seriously, no quick travel for a sandbox game like this? Fall damage sucks ass too, I drop a height of the player maybe and you lose half your hp bar, like bro I could fall that much in real life and maybe I'd have a sprained ankle, not broken 20 bones. Positives: It's unique for the 3d Noita feel with the runes and the spell combining, and the bones are there, I really do expect changes in my negatives and patches to fix all this, but it just feels so far off right now. I definitely will buy the game again in the future but this is what I feel now.

A simple dungeon crawl game with an interesting rune magic system. Difficulty is a bit lackluster on Normal. It only took me two attempts. With the right runes, bosses can easily be killed in under a second, before they even have a chance to attack. With the wrong runes, you can easily crash the game from the sheer number of particles bouncing around the room. All in all, the game has some interesting mechanics and is fun. It feels like the bones of a very good game are here. It's pretty solid for what it is, but feels in need of further expansion.

Runehaven is a voxel roguelike. [b]Story[/b] 1/10 Completely nonexistent. [b]Playtime:[/b] 5/10 It takes about 3 hours to try out most of the mechanics, and around 10 hours to see absolutely everything the game has to offer. [b]The Short Answer: Is It Worth Buying?[/b] I’d say it’s worth picking up, but grab it on a sale. [b]Mechanics and Gameplay[/b] 7/10 At its core, it’s a standard physical roguelike with fully destructible environments. Think of it as a 3D version of Noita. The game’s standout, unique mechanic is its enchantment system: you can apply buffs to any weapon by literally drawing a rune. There's a solid variety here, with about 40 different runes to discover. As for the arsenal, there are around 9 weapon classes, totaling about 40–50 individual weapons. When it comes to the gameplay loop, the core mechanic of having to go all the way down and then climb back up felt incredibly tedious. The map layout itself is pretty mediocre, though it does feature a lot of hidden areas you can blow open and explore. [b]Enemies and Bosses[/b] 4/10 The enemy variety spans from simple skeletons to some highly annoying mobs. The bosses, unfortunately, don't feel special—they are just upscaled versions of regular enemies. [b]Graphics:[/b] 3/10 Voxel style. [b]Music:[/b] 4/10 Wait, did this game even have music? [b]Personal Take[/b] The game is admittedly kind of cool, but it suffers from a massive lack of purpose. You just keep moving forward without ever really knowing why you're doing it. On top of that, the in-run shops feel very weird, and there is a handful of consumables that I finished the game without ever figuring out what they were actually meant for. [b]Overall Score:[/b] 61/100

Despite the main spell-drawing gimmick, the game does not offer much in terms of variety and experimentation. There is no need to pick and choose your runes, because in later stages you have so many slots for a single spell you can just use them all. Why experiment, when you can just craft a Spread-Exploding-Seeking-Earthly-Lifesteal-Manasteal magic missile, and kill every enemy in one shot (or three shots if its a boss). I really wish there was more reason to use weird, wacky spells lie the ones that make you magic missiles heavier or slower, or return towards you, but as it stands you would be using them only as some sort of self-imposed challenge. TL;DR: despite great amount of runes to collect and craft spells with, there is no spell variety
